result.notes:
Blocking review item fixed: BOM overrides now follow the part (T-217).

Root cause: overrides were keyed only by refdes. Re-keying them in the update_part_properties handler cannot work, because undo/redo replay ECS patches (replaceSchematicProjection) past every handler. So each override row is now bound to the schematic part id, which is also the placement's partId and is kept across undo/redo.

- **Migration 0019** rebuilds `designer_bom_overrides`, following the assistant 0005 table-rebuild precedent. The old inline `unique(design_id, refdes)` had to go: a renamed part's row keeps its old refdes, and another part may now carry it. The rebuilt table adds `part_id`, which is backfilled from `designer_schematic_parts` by (design_id, reference). New indexes: `unique(design_id, part_id)`, and `unique(design_id, refdes) WHERE part_id IS NULL`.
- **Upsert**: resolves the URL refdes to the part carrying it now. It updates that part's bound row, or adopts an unbound row under that refdes, or inserts a new one. A refdes that no schematic part carries (a PCB-only placement) keeps an unbound row matched by refdes, as before.
- **Writer**: matches a bound override by partId only, so a stale refdes can never land on another part. An unbound override matches by refdes and never beats a bound one.
- **PnP**: excludes DNP parts by placementId.

Reviewer's probe, now a test: DNP+LCSC on C1, rename to C77 → pnp.csv = [C2] and the C77 BOM row has dnp=true and keeps its LCSC. Undo → excluded under C1. Redo → excluded under C77. Then C2 is renamed to the freed C1: it does not inherit the override, a new PATCH on C1 binds to C2 with no UNIQUE collision, and C77 keeps its data.

Known, acceptable leftover: a legacy row the migration could not bind still matches by refdes, which is the old behaviour. A deleted part's bound row stays in the table so undoing the delete brings it back; it never applies to any other part.

The running bun --watch backends will apply 0019 to their databases on restart. Memory note designer-batch-derived-refs.md is updated: the stale "overrides keyed by refdes" line is replaced with the part_id binding facts.
reviewNotes: T-217 migration (0019_bom_override_part_binding.sql:52-57): the backfill binds a row only when a schematic part carries its refdes at upgrade time. Designs that already hit the T-217 bug can have an override (often DNP) written on the phantom stale-placement line, e.g. 'R1' after R1 was renamed to R7. That row stays unbound, so it no longer reaches the physical part: R7 goes back into pnp.csv, where the old code excluded it through the stale placement ref. It can also be inherited silently by a future part that gets auto-annotated 'R1'. Suggestion: fall back to the stale placement's reference (json_extract of the designer_pcb_entities placement payload's reference/partId) before leaving a row unbound.

0019 copies rows into a table with a FOREIGN KEY on designer_design_heads while foreign keys are ON. A legacy override row whose design is gone would abort the migration, and the backend would then fail to start. store.ts:515 deletes overrides on design delete and the FK cascades, so this is unlikely. A `where o.design_id in (select id from designer_design_heads)` guard would make it bulletproof.

bom-overrides.ts: a bound row whose part is permanently deleted is never cleaned up. It stays inert in the BOM and is listed by listBomOverrides under its old refdes. That is harmless because no consumer keys overrides by refdes any more, but the rows pile up.

bom-overrides.ts:42-60: PATCH /bom/refs/:refdes with a reference nobody carries (e.g. a BOM view that has not refreshed after a rename) returns 200 and writes an inert unbound row (partId null), so the user's edit silently goes nowhere. Before this change that was only possible for truly unknown refs. Consider a 404/409 when the refdes matches neither a schematic part nor a placement.

T-162: boards imported before this change can carry duplicate net-class ids. Saving the Design rules dialog on them is now refused outright ('duplicate id') and nothing self-heals it. The contract documents this, but such a board cannot save any rule edit until a duplicate row is removed. commit.ts uniqueId fixes new imports only.

T-164: the brief suggested appending a short id when two designs' names collide. The contract drops that, so two designs with the same name export identically named bundles. The approved scope (named after the design name) is met.
pcb-helpers.ts:31 has literal combining characters in the regex /[̀-ͯ]/. They are correct (U+0300–U+036F), but an escaped form (̀-ͯ) would be readable and editor-safe.

Batch (commands/batch.ts): dataset capture tags a batch as opKinds {batch_commands:1}, so per-step pcb_* capture semantics are lost for batched PCB edits. This does not matter for current callers because autolayout apply is not batchable.

crossOwner.need: Page the table/grid using GET /components?offset=&limit= (max 200). Response data is now {components,total,offset,limit}. Use total for the header count and the 'n of total' strip, load more until offset>=total, and make Select All either say it covers loaded rows only or fetch every page first. Replace Space.tsx limit=60. See contracts/LB.md.

The facet mount keys are now canonical smd/tht/mixed (they were the raw through_hole). The list and the facets now share one predicate, so list.total === facets.total. Humanise the mount labels in the UI if wanted. Free text no longer searches the source id.

Each clone now owns its footprint ids, so STEP upload to the copy's effectiveSelectedId works as-is. canUploadStep can stay !isBuiltin. Optionally show the Details 'Source' row from the new component.origin (a copy has origin.componentId !== id). The backend guard text now says 'Duplicate to edit'.

An installed pack is never kind 'core' now: a missing or spoofed kind is stored as 'team', removable and not read-only. POST /sources/install with the reserved id openpcb.core or user.local returns 409 (type library-source-reserved). Surface that error.

result.notes:
All six LB entries are fixed at their root. Backend work is done; the frontend owners still have their parts (see crossOwner). Nothing was committed.

**What changed, by entry**
- **T-253 (list and facets disagree):**
  - New module `backend/component-filter.ts` is the one predicate for both GET /components and GET /facets.
  - Free-text search covers name, description and tags. The source id is no longer searched.
  - Mount is canonicalised to smd/tht/mixed. It comes from the default footprint's mountType plus any mount tags. MOUNT_TAGS now also accepts through_hole, thru_hole, pth and mixed.
  - System tags filter the same way in both endpoints.
  - Checked against the committed core pack: all=17/17, q=passive 3/3, q=R 17/17, tags=smd 13/13, tht 4/4, through_hole 4/4, ic+smd 4/4 (list/facets).
- **T-256 (list truncated at 60):**
  - GET /components takes `offset`. The response is `{components, total, offset, limit}`; `data.components` is unchanged, so existing readers keep working.
  - Max page size went from 100 to 200. A negative or non-numeric offset returns 400.
  - Order is stable: exact name, then name prefix, then name contains, then other matches; ties by name, then id. Searching R puts a part named R first.
  - The SDK `searchComponents` signature is unchanged. It now wraps the new `searchComponentsPage`.
- **T-270 (Duplicate to edit):**
  - `cloneComponent` runs in one transaction. It copies every footprint-option row (label, default flag, order, pin map) and the metadata columns: manufacturer, MPN, LCSC, supplier, subcategory, datasheet URL, keywords.
  - It deep-copies each footprint row and its 3D-model row into user.local under new ids. The GLB/STEP files are content-addressed and ref-counted, so sharing them is safe. The copy therefore owns its footprints and STEP upload works.
  - `deleteComponents` now also collects and orphan-checks option footprints, so deleting a copy removes its private footprints.
  - A new optional field, `LibraryComponent.origin`, lets the frontend show the Source row.
  - Guard messages now say "Duplicate to edit" instead of "Duplicate to my library".
- **T-049 (no-kind pack became read-only core):**
  - The stored kind comes from `sync/source-ids.ts`: 'core' only for the id openpcb.core; a declared 'user' stays; anything else becomes 'team'. isReadOnly follows that.
  - Migration 0011 repairs existing bad rows.
- **T-055 (user.local removable):** `deleteSource` now refuses openpcb.core and user.local by id with 409 problem+json (type library-source-protected). Source rows gain `isRemovable`.
- **T-251 (500 on invalid files):** the inspect-kicad shim maps the parsers' plain Error (not subclasses such as TypeError) to ImportValidationError, so the endpoint returns 400 problem+json instead of 500. The shim is also used by the commit and zip import paths; only the inspect path is covered by a test.

**Where I departed from the brief**
- (a) A pack with a missing or 'core' kind becomes 'team', not 'third-party': the @openpcb/opclib-pack kind union is core|user|team, and the brief's detail text says 'team'.
- (b) The core delete refusal changed from 400 to 409, so core and user.local share one protected-source problem type. I updated the existing test.
- (c) Added: POST /sources/install now refuses the reserved ids openpcb.core and user.local with 409. Otherwise a user pack with either id would become unremovable, and the user.local case would wipe the user's parts through reconcileSourceRows.
- (d) The clone copies footprints but keeps the symbol shared. Nothing edits symbols in place, so a copy is not needed for the approved scope.

**Accident, cleaned up:** I ran `npm run sdk:generate`. Its scripts:build step fails with TS6059 but still wrote 165 untracked .js files next to .ts sources under src/. All were timestamped by that run, all had a .ts sibling, and none were tracked. I deleted them, so the tree is back to its prior state. `npm run gen` itself is safe. I recorded this in agent memory.

**Follow-ups I noticed but did not fix**
- `importOpclib` still throws plain Error for signature and asset failures, which gives 500 on /sources/install.
- `deleteSource` answers 'source not found' as 400; it should be 404.
- List and facets parse every footprint's dataJson on every request. That is fine at the current library size; `json_extract` could replace it later.
- `deleteComponents` never deletes GLB files on disk; only the model rows cascade.
- A clone keeps the 'core' tag, because only builtin/system tags are stripped.
- In a full `bun test` run, `library-opclib-bootstrap.test.ts` deletes OPENPCB_BUNDLED_LIBRARY_PATH in its afterEach.
reviewNotes: T-270, migration path: duplicates made before this change are not repaired. They still share core footprints and lack the extra footprint options, pin maps and metadata. STEP upload on them still fails with 'Cannot update built-in components (…). Use "Duplicate to edit"…' while the user is on a duplicate (assertFootprintNotBuiltinComponent, queries.ts:1410). A one-off repair, or forking the footprint on write for non-builtin callers, would remove that dead end for existing user DBs.

T-270: the copy still shares its symbol. For a duplicate of an installed pack part, deleteSource (queries.ts, `txDb.delete(symbols).where(eq(symbols.sourceId, sourceId))`) removes the pack's symbols without checking references. Removing the pack then leaves the copy in user.local with a dangling symbolId (components.symbol_id has no FK). This existed before; the fix narrowed it by making footprints private but did not close it.

T-049, trust boundary: the reserved-id guard lives only in installOpclibFromBytes (install-source.ts). cloud-sync.ts pullCustomLibrary calls importOpclib directly with requireSignature:false, so a cloud-served pack with id openpcb.core would still get kind core and isBuiltin=1. Separately, the importer updates components by entity id and sets sourceId/isBuiltin from the pack (opclib-importer.ts ~750). A foreign pack whose component ids collide with openpcb.core.* can take over core rows, and removing that pack later deletes them. Both existed before and are outside the brief, but they are next to its 'only the bundled core can be core' goal.

Perf: GET /components now loads every component and JSON-parses every default footprint's dataJson on each request (about 2.2 MB of footprint JSON for 227 components in the dev DB). GET /facets already did this, so each search keystroke now pays for it twice. Before, the unfiltered list was limited in SQL. Fine at current library sizes; worth caching mountType if user libraries grow into the thousands.
parseOffset (routes.ts:1149) uses parseInt, so '10abc' is accepted as 10 and '1.5' as 1. The contract says non-numeric input gives 400; only fully non-numeric or negative values do.

translatePackageError (import/inspect-kicad.ts) now maps every plain `Error` from @openpcb/kicad-import to 400. That is right for parser rejects, but an internal invariant failure thrown as a plain Error in the package would also be reported as a user-input 400 instead of a 500.

New sync/source-ids.ts does not consolidate existing duplicates: bootstrap.ts:17 still has its own USER_LOCAL_SOURCE_ID, core-library-updates.ts:14 its own CORE_SOURCE_ID, and opclib-importer.ts keeps the literal 'openpcb.core' at :193, :290, :707.
cloneComponent (queries.ts ~1449-1532) is about 80 lines, above the protocol's under-50 guideline. Most of it is one insert values object, so this is minor.

Existing test-infrastructure problems, unrelated to LB but relevant to the orchestrator's gate run: (a) CoreLibrary/dist/openpcb-core-library-0.0.0-dev.opclib has more than 500 ZIP entries, so the bundled core fails to load in default test runs; (b) batch `bun test library-` has cross-file env leakage (OPENPCB_BUNDLED_LIBRARY_PATH reset by afterEach), which causes 16-18 failures that pass per file.
